source_span: the move being driven by real yields... 10yr US real yields rising +9.8bps to a post-2008 high of 2.87% but 10yr breakevens actually falling by -1.3bps
source_chain: Oil spikes and resilient growth data (jobless claims, home sales) push yields to multi-decade highs, therefore decomposing the move shows breakevens flat-to-lower while real yields did nearly all the work (+9.8bp to 2.87%, +97bp YTD vs +9bp for breakevens) and term premium has sat flat 18 months, therefore at face value there is no inflation-compensation story despite oil up ~75%, with Reid's own bias that breakevens are too low / real yields too high (no hard trigger given).
pulse_chain: Yields hit multi-decade highs in the fastest 2-day move since Liberation Day, therefore the same decomposition (real yields +9.8bp to 2.87% vs breakevens -1.3bp, term premium flat 18 months) shows it's a growth/real-yield story not inflation or deficits, reinforced by mechanical selling (weak 5-year auction, light buyback takeup) and set against a GS-vs-BofA position debate, with Goldman's own speed-rule (50bp/month or 30bp/2wk trigger, currently ~35bp/25bp) as the falsifiable condition, cut against near-max CTA shorts that could force a squeeze instead.
why: The pulse reproduces Reid's real-yield-vs-breakeven decomposition and figures in the same direction without reversing or misattributing it, and layers in a different note's own explicitly-sourced invalidation (Goldman's speed rule) rather than swapping out Reid's argument for an invented one.
